lines.text: Forty-three instruments, laid out three ways. These are design layouts, not built labs.
First, a conventional materials lab, grouped by workflow: rooms for powder, the metal printers, the machine shop, the furnace and the SEM, and open benches for the rest.
Benches are thirty inches deep and aisles five feet wide, with service space behind every floor machine. Measured to its walls, it comes to 4,280 square feet.
Next, the same floor plan, automated. Mobile robots drive the routes people walked, with fixed arms, docking targets and sample racks at the stations.
The floor area stays the same. And a robot docked in a five-foot aisle leaves too little room for another to pass.
The vertical lab. Two Kardex Shuttles come in, and every benchtop instrument moves onto a tray.
The floor machines rearrange along one robot aisle, and the floor area falls to 3,029 square feet.
Side by side, the vertical lab needs 29 percent less floor: 14.2 instruments per thousand square feet, against 10.0.
Laid out so robots can dock and pass, a flat lab needs 4,128 square feet. And by capacity, the Shuttles hold 45 trays: 14.9 tray positions per thousand square feet, against 7.3 laid out flat.

In the vertical lab, most of the floor goes to the floor machines, their clearances and the robot aisle, the same as in the flat layouts for robots. And the Shuttles stand 9.15 meters tall, so it needs a high bay.
For scale, Emerald Cloud Lab in South San Francisco held more than a hundred items of equipment in about 15,000 square feet.

conventional.name: conventional
conventional.title: Conventional lab
notes: Zones along a 6 ft corridor; each zone's back row against its far wall, its front row against the corridor wall, a 5 ft aisle between them.

flat.name: flat
flat.title: Automated, same floor plan
notes: 4 mobile manipulators; 24 docking targets; 5 fixed arms, each with a sample rack; 2 chargers. A docked MiR250 (580 mm wide) leaves 0.94 m of a 5 ft aisle: less than the 1.45 m one needs to drive by, so robots wait in the aisles.

robots.name: robots
robots.title: Automated, laid out for robots
notes: 18 tray-sized bench positions (18 with today's trays): 2 where the Shuttles stood, facing the MiR aisle; 16 in 4 rows of up to 4, 2 one-way 1.45 m MiR aisles with an 838 mm dock lane each side, cross-aisles at both ends; the floor machines as in the vertical lab.

vertical.name: vertical
vertical.title: Vertical lab
notes: North row: glovebox, atomizer, sieving cell, two Shuttles, LPBF. South row: two Instrons, three chargers, fume hood, DED, wire EDM, packaging. East end: EOS M 400-4 and Meltio cell (no MiR dock).
